raw_text:
Here is a concise, battle-ready 12-week summary you can share with your client or drop into a planning doc. It combines the four 3-week phase structure (Phase 1: Foundation, Phase 2: Push/Progress, Phase 3: Strength with tempo, Phase 4: Peak/Consolidation), plus the added Saturday finisher, mobility routine, nutrition, cardio, and equipment guidance we’ve discussed. It’s tailored for a 27-year-old beginner training in a small flat with a yoga mat and a doorway pull-up bar, with 4 training days per week and optional cardio, finishers, and mobility days.

Overall plan at a glance
- Duration: 12 weeks
- Frequency: 4 strength days per week (A: Push, B: Pull, C: Lower, D: Full Body/Hybrid) + optional Saturday finisher + mobility 3–4 times/week + cardio 2–3 times/week + nutrition plan
- Equipment: bodyweight, doorway pull-up bar, minimal equipment (begins with bodyweight; add bands/dumbbells/kettlebell as you progress)
- Progression principle: simple, safe overload through tempo, leverage/variation, reps, and occasional light external load. Regressions provided if form or recovery falters.

Phases overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Foundation and technique
  - Focus: Learn patterns, establish habit, build base work capacity, correct mechanics
  - Typical structure: 4 classic bodyweight days with gradual progression; emphasis on form, light volume
  - Accessory: core and mobility emphasis; core work included in each week
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Progressive overload on push and pulling
  - Focus: increase pushing load and introduce tempo/weighted variations (using backpack, dumbbells, or bands)
  - Push intensity emphasized; maintain form and appropriate volume
  - Progression: tempo, elevation/decline variations, added load
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Strength emphasis with tempo and higher resistance
  - Focus: controlled tempo, more challenging variations, stable technique at higher effort
  - Progression: maintain volume with stricter tempo; more demanding push/pull/hinge patterns
- Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Peak strength and consolidation
  - Focus: peak effort while maintaining technique; final tests and deload
  - Week 12: deload and optional testing of metrics (max reps, time to stand, etc.)

Weekly structure (core)
- Day A: Push (upper body)
- Day B: Pull (upper body)
- Day C: Lower (legs/glutes/core)
- Day D: Full body / Hybrid (strength + conditioning emphasis)
- Cardio: 2–3 sessions per week (templates provided)
- Mobility: 3–4 sessions per week (short routines; can be slotted before/after workouts)
- Saturday Finisher: Optional 20–25 minute fun finisher (rotate between options)
- Rest: 1–2 minutes between sets; 2–3 minutes for heavy/compound sets

Phase 1: Weeks 1–3 – Foundation and technique
- Goals: Patterning, technique mastery, establish baseline, build work capacity
- Sample weekly outline (example you can adapt):
  - Day A Push: Bodyweight push variants; incline/decline progression; core finisher
  - Day B Pull: Doorway rows, negatives or assisted pull-ups, hangs
  - Day C Lower: Squats, glute bridges, lunges, core
  - Day D Full Body/Conditioning: burpees (scaled), hip thrusts, carries, mobility
- Reps/sets: Begin with 3x6–12 per exercise, progress by 1–2 reps weekly; add tempo (2-0-2) on lowering phases
- Mobility: 3–4 sessions per week, 8–12 minutes, focused on thoracic spine, hips, ankles, shoulders

Phase 2: Weeks 4–6 – Progressive overload on push
- Focus: Increase pushing load; tempo work; introduction of weighted variants
- Push progression (examples): elevated feet push-ups, pike push-ups, chair dips with tempo, dumbbell/ backpack press or floor press
- Pull/Lower maintained with progressive overload where possible
- Sample target framework for Day A Push (Weeks 4–6): 4x6–9 (varies by week), include 1–2 tempo sets; 3x8–10 for accessory
- Cardio: 2 sessions/week (Templates A/B recommended)
- Saturday Finisher: rotate options; keep it 15–25 minutes
- Nutrition: maintain protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg, modest surplus 250–350 kcal above maintenance; adjust after 2–3 weeks based on progress

Phase 3: Weeks 7–9 – Strength emphasis with tempo control
- Focus: true strength with controlled tempo; more demanding variations
- Push/pull/legs: deeper tempos, longer eccentrics; introduce near-peak resistance within volumes
- Example adjustments: decline push-ups, elevated push variants, heavier dumbbell loads, slower tempo on rows and presses
- Cardio: maintain 2–3 sessions; consider one longer (20–30 min) session if energy allows
- Mobility: maintain routine to protect shoulders and hips

Phase 4: Weeks 10–12 – Peak strength and consolidation
- Focus: peak effort with quality reps; consolidate gains; deload in Week 12
- Week 10–11: push/pull/legs at higher intensity with refined technique
- Week 12: 40–50% volume deload; optional testing (push-ups max reps, pull-ups max reps, squats max reps)
- Saturday Finisher: switch to lighter, more playful options if fatigue is present
- Nutrition: monitor weight changes; adjust calories to maintain lean gains or stay near maintenance depending on goals; keep protein targets stable

Cardio plan (2–3 sessions per week)
- Template A (Weeks 1–3): 12–20 minutes easy cardio; low impact; progression to 18–20 minutes by Week 4
- Template B (Weeks 4–6): 15–25 minutes circuit or intervals (low-to-moderate intensity)
- Template C (Weeks 7–9): 20–30 minutes steady or short intervals
- Template D (Weeks 10–12): 20–40 minutes optional longer cardio if energy allows
- Intensity cues: primarily RPE 5–6/10; intervals at RPE 7–8 for short bursts

Nutrition plan (brief recap)
- Calorie target: modest surplus +250–350 kcal above maintenance (adjust after 2–3 weeks)
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg target daily; distribute across 4–5 meals
- Carbs: aligned with training days for energy; fats fill remaining calories
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L/day; adjust for activity level
- Breakfast/Lunch/Dinner/Snacks: balanced protein+carbs+fats; pre/post-workout nutrition around training
- Monitoring: weigh-ins weekly; adjust calories downward if gaining fat too fast; upward if strength and size stall

Saturday Finisher options (rotate weekly; 20–25 minutes)
- Playful burn circuits
- Time-lenced mini-challenges (AMRAP rounds)
- Dance-based cardio finishers
- Quick PR-aim sessions (aim to beat last week’s reps)

Mobility routine (3–4 days/week; 10–15 minutes)
- Warm-up: 2–3 minutes dynamic
- Mobility blocks: thoracic spine, shoulders, hips, ankles, spine decompression
- Activation/stability: glute bridges, bird-dogs, planks as needed
- Cool-down breathing: 1–2 minutes
- Schedule: integrate on non-intensive days or as cool-downs after workouts

Weekly planning notes
- Rest days: active recovery (light walking, gentle mobility) recommended
- Monitoring: keep a simple log for sets, reps, tempo, and RPE; track weight weekly
- Adaptations: regress moves if pain occurs; swap to incline/assisted variants
- Equipment: phase progression can be achieved with bodyweight and minimal added load; add resistance bands/dumbbells/kettlebell only when ready

What to deliver to client (ready-to-use)
- 12-week calendar with Week-by-week sessions and exact day-by-day workouts
- Phase-specific progressions (Phase 1, Phase 2, Phase 3, Phase 4)
- Sample Day A/B/C/D workouts for Weeks 1–12 with sets, reps, tempos
- Saturday finisher schedule (rotate 4 options; Week-by-week)
- Mobility plan (3–4 days/week with daily blocks and durations)
- Cardio plan (2–3 sessions/week with templates A–C)
- Nutrition quick-start: calorie target ranges, protein targets, and 7-day meal plan template
- Progress tracking sheet: weight, reps, performance notes, energy, sleep

Would you like me to convert this into a precise, week-by-week calendar (Weeks 1–12) with exact workouts for each day, including the four-week rotation for Saturday finisher and the exact cardio/mobility templates? If you share the client’s approximate weight, height, and any dietary restrictions or equipment specifics (do you plan to use bands, dumbbells, kettlebell, or just bodyweight?), I can tailor the plan even more precisely and generate printable schedules, checklists, and a simple nutrition log aligned with the plan.
